title: Publish optional headless Docker/OCI image
notes: This task's owner override (MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md, MBR-910) reads: 'The OCI image supports manually exercised headless Linux/server evaluation. CI integration and workflow configuration are out of scope and forbidden.' No .github/workflows/**, CI, or hosted/self-hosted runner configuration was added or touched.

packaging/oci/Containerfile, packaging/oci/release.v1.json, scripts/release/verify-oci-release.mjs, and tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs already existed on main (commit b7b01a8f, 'feat(distribution): add optional OCI source contract') as a deliberately fail-closed source contract: state 'unavailable', publish:false, all-zero placeholder digests, and every evidence slot null. This task's job, now that MBR-903 has landed (commit 3811091e, scripts/release/pipeline/multi-platform-release.mjs), was to add the missing piece that scaffold could not have had before MBR-903 existed: a real, tested binding from that OCI contract to an actual MBR-903 release identity plus real per-artifact evidence -- not to re-author the contract or its validator.

New: scripts/release/oci/generate-oci-release.mjs (new subdirectory, per this task's allowed paths). It is the only supported way to move packaging/oci/release.v1.json from 'unavailable' to 'ready'. It reads an existing evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json (MBR-903's own immutable record; refuses to proceed if it does not exist, is not exactly that schema, is not publish:false, or its releaseId does not recompute from its own app/version/commit -- catching a hand-edited record), copies identity.tag/commit/release_generation from it verbatim, requires --base to match packaging/oci/Containerfile's FROM line (catching drift between the contract and what was actually built), requires a real Linux membrane binary (--binary) and hashes it itself for identity.artifact_sha256, requires five real evidence files (--sbom --ed25519 --cosign --rootless-health --secret-scan) and hashes each itself, then hands the assembled candidate to the PRE-EXISTING, UNMODIFIED scripts/release/verify-oci-release.mjs#verifyOciRelease as the single source of truth before writing anything. Any missing/invalid input fails closed and leaves release.v1.json untouched. A second write with a genuinely different candidate for an already-'ready' release is refused, not silently overwritten (mirrors MBR-903's writeImmutableReleaseGeneration idempotency contract).

Reused, unmodified, via import only (all outside this task's allowed paths): scripts/release/verify-oci-release.mjs#verifyOciRelease (the validator itself -- not reimplemented); scripts/release/pipeline/identity.mjs's HEX40/HEX64/TAG regexes; scripts/release/pipeline/multi-platform-release.mjs#releaseId (used to cross-check a release-generation record's own releaseId field against its app/version/commit).

Fixed a real defect found while reading the pre-existing scaffold, within this task's own packaging/oci/** allowlist: the Containerfile's HEALTHCHECK ran `membrane health --headless`, a CLI invocation that does not exist anywhere in engine/crates/membrane -- a plausible-looking fake, exactly what this task's hard rules forbid inventing. Replaced with `membrane cli doctor paths`, a real, read-only, non-interactive diagnostic (engine/crates/membrane/src/modes.rs's is_doctor_paths_invocation/run_doctor_paths, covered by that crate's own dispatch.rs/modes.rs tests) that resolves Membrane's four stable roots and prints JSON, exiting 0 via DispatchOutcome::Ok (engine/crates/membrane/src/main.rs). tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs's matching assertion was updated to the new, real command; a new test in that same file asserts the Containerfile carries no EXPOSE directive (no network service exposed by default), backing this task's local-first/loopback-bound requirement.

docs/install-oci.md (new file, per this task's allowed paths -- docs/install.md itself belongs to a landed lane and was read but not modified) documents: what the image is/is not (never a Linux desktop-app substitute), the explicit no-CI-forbidden note, that docs/support-matrix.json currently backs zero platforms/clients (every row 'unavailable', generatedFrom.releaseGeneration null) so this image claims no support tier, exactly how identity.mjs binding works end to end with the real CLI invocation, and the declared gaps below.

Declared gaps, not fabricated: (1) no image has ever been built, signed, or pushed -- packaging/oci/release.v1.json remains state:'unavailable' on disk after this task, exactly as before; (2) release/contracts/platforms.v1.json's four logical release targets have no 'linux' entry and this task does not add one (that file is outside MBR-910's allowlist) -- the OCI image binds to the same source identity as the desktop builds via release-generation.json, but is not a RightKit-sealed platform target; (3) no SBOM/signing/cosign/secret-scan tool (syft/cosign/trivy or similar) was installed or invoked -- generate-oci-release.mjs only validates and hashes evidence files an operator already produced elsewhere; (4) `membrane cli doctor paths` is a real but general read-only diagnostic, not an app-specific liveness probe -- documented as a declared limitation, not oversold.

No cargo, pnpm, Tauri, right-release, docker, podman, buildah, cosign, syft, or any signing command was run. No mutating git command (add/commit/checkout/stash/reset/rebase/push) was run. Only `node --test tests/oci/generate-oci-release.test.mjs` and `node --test tests/oci/oci-contract.test.mjs` (the two test files this task wrote/modified) were executed -- see commands.log. No .github/workflows/** or other CI/workflow configuration was added, per this task's explicit owner override.
